subject: Dedicated capacity options and activation plan for Argo Health
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@argohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal for Argo Health — options and recommended path

Hi Jamie —

Appreciate the time yesterday. Based on the forecast you shared (peak inference across claims routing + chat assistants, ~85% tail load spikes), we modeled three dedicated reservation structures that align to your throughput needs and budget flexibility. Attached is a PDF with the line-item pricing; below are the activation/ramp sketches and our recommendation.

Summary of options (quick):

1) Conservative onramp (Recommended for risk-managed launch)
   - Cluster: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline)
   - Min guaranteed: 16 GPUs (reserved floor)
   - Ramp: active weeks 1–8: 16 -> 24 GPUs; week 9–12: 24 -> 32 GPUs
   - Canary window: 14 days prior to week 1 on limited traffic
   - Warm-up credits: 48 hours free burst + caching warm-up (included)

2) Growth-first (faster time-to-capacity)
   - Cluster: 64 GPUs
   - Min guaranteed: 32 GPUs
   - Ramp: 30 days to full capacity with staged activation (8–16–32–64)
   - Reduced per-token unit price at 64 GPU commit

3) Headroom-ready (peak-sensitive, shorter latency SLOs)
   - Cluster: 128 GPUs with auto-burst lane to 160 for sustained spikes
   - Min guaranteed: 64 GPUs
   - Ramp: 60-day activation, reserved burst contract for scheduled events

Key engineering trade-offs:
- Lower min guarantees keep committed spend small but increase risk of throttling under extreme tail bursts (we provide automatic fallback to hosted tier).
- Higher cluster sizes reduce unit cost and improve tail latency but require longer activation windows and higher upfront commit.

Operational items we recommend including in the SOW:
- Canary and pilot traffic profile (we'll provide a one-week test harness)
- KV prefix caching setup and recommended batching targets per endpoint
- A 12-week activation playbook with rollback triggers and traffic cutover checklist

I've attached the proposal (redwood-dedicated-proposal-argo-v2.pdf) and a sample activation schedule (gpu-activation-schedule-argo.xlsx). Marissa/Ben — added you for SRE/ops input on the playbook.

Next steps: 1) Let me know which option you'd like priced against a 12- or 24-month commitment; 2) any procurement constraints we should bake into the proposal (SLA, audit logs, on-prem options).

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference platform
From: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@argohealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@argohealth.com>, Argo Health Solutions Team <solutions@argohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal for Argo Health — options and recommended path

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- We like the Conservative onramp as a starting point, but we need a shorter canary (7 days) and a clearly defined rollback SLA if latency regressions exceed 2x for more than 6 hours.
- For pricing: can you show the delta between 12- and 18-month commitments? Our finance team is pushing for an 18-month to smooth budget, but procurement may push back.
- On the Min guaranteed: would you accept a graduated floor (8 GPUs first month -> 16 next) to limit initial cash flow?

Attach: internal traffic forecast (argo-forecast-dec24.csv) — forwarding to procurement.

Jamie Lowe
VP Product, Argo Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@argohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal for Argo Health — options and recommended path

Hi Jamie —

Thanks — quick operational response from our side. We can accommodate a graduated floor as you suggest with these constraints: the billing floor and activation triggers are explicit (we invoice the minimum that is active at the start of each billing month). Proposed graduated floor path: month 1 = 8 GPUs reserved + 16 GPU burst pool; month 2 = 16 GPUs reserved; month 3 = 24; month 4 = full 32 (if you pick the 32-cluster option).

Canary tightening: 7-day canary is fine; we'll run a blackbox latency monitor and provide hourly SLI dashboards during the window. Rollback SLA: we can include automated rollback to hosted fallback within 60 minutes if latency/regression thresholds are met and the customer approves the automated trigger. Legal will want the exact thresholds written into the SOW.

Operational asks for Argo to prepare before pilot:
- A list of 5 representative endpoints and sample payload sizes
- Peak QPS estimate for the canary window
- Single point of contact for cutover and incident comms

Ben — can you confirm the lead SRE for activation and the warm-up credit allocation?

Marissa
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement <procurement@argohealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@argohealth.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@argohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal for Argo Health — options and recommended path

Karthik —

PROCUREMENT NOTES (please route to sales/legal):

1) We prefer the graduated floor but would like the initial month reserved minimum to be 12 GPUs (not 8). Can you show a price table with 12 -> 20 -> 28 -> 32 progression?
2) SLA exceptions: our legal team will request uptime language for the reserved pool and a 45-day credit window for demonstrated SLA breaches. We will also require SOC2 Type II evidence and network diagrams for VPC peering.
3) Ramp window: procurement asks for a 90-day soft ramp with defined check-ins every 30 days; we can agree to an 18-month term on that cadence pending final pricing.

Please include a DocuSign-ready SOW and a reference to the activation checklist.

Procurement Team
Argo Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@argohealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@argohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal for Argo Health — options and recommended path

Jamie / Procurement —

Appreciate the notes and the preferred path. Per the ask, I've updated the attached pricing sheet to include a 12/20/28/32 graduated-reservation table, and an 18-month term option; see redwood-dedicated-proposal-argo-v2.pdf and gpu-activation-schedule-argo.xlsx for the linked schedule. High-level confirmation of what we'll put in the SOW:

- Agreed reservation ladder: month 1 = 12 GPUs reserved (+ burst pool 20), month 2 = 20 reserved, month 3 = 28 reserved, month 4 = 32 reserved (full cluster).
- 90-day soft ramp with 30-day review checkpoints and named Redwood SRE point-of-contact (Marissa).
- Canary: 7 days with hourly SLI reporting; rollback automation to hosted fallback within 60 minutes if threshold breach confirmed.
- SLA/credits: Redwood accepts 45-day credit remediation for verified reserved-pool SLA breaches; SOC2 Type II evidence and VPC network diagrams attached.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm the 12 -> 20 -> 28 -> 32 ladder and sign the DocuSign SOW we will circulate today.
2) Redwood will schedule a pre-pilot technical readiness call (Marissa + SRE) and share the playbook.

If procurement prefers, we can also present a 24-month pricing table with slightly lower unit rates — call it out and we'll include that in the DocuSign package.

Thanks and happy holidays —
Karthik
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-argo-v2.pdf (proposal), gpu-activation-schedule-argo.xlsx (activation schedule), redwood-soc2-type2-summary.pdf (compliance snapshot)
